newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia 96/97 coffee output seen hit by weather.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia 96/97 coffee output seen hit by weather.

text.p: Indonesia's coffee production is expected to be 10 to 15 percent below the projected 480,000 tonnes in the 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) coffee year due to bad weather, the chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters, Oesman Soedargo, said on Thursday.

He also said Indonesia was "open to discussion" on a move by the InterAfrican Coffee Organisation (IACO) to get members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) to cut exports by 2.5 million 60-kg bags in the first half of 1997.

"We did a survey of highlands on Sumatra and found that the flowering process has been affected by heavy rainfall," Soedargo told Reuters in an interview. "Just-developing beans had also dropped off because of strong winds."
"I expect a 10-to-15 percent drop from our earlier forecast of 480,000 tonnes," he said.
Soedargo also said Indonesia had yet to make a decision on the African initiative to cut coffee exports in the first half of this year, but added that it was open to discussion.
"The difference in the prices of Robusta and Arabica coffee is of concern to us, and I will raise this issue at the ACPC meeting in Brazil next week," he said.
The 14-member ACPC will hold an emergency meeting in Brazil to discuss coffee prices, and is expected to explore the African proposal whose success hinges on Indonesian participation.

Indonesia, the world's third largest coffee producer after Brazil and Colombia, has been reluctant to back the African proposal because its trade rival Vietnam is not an ACPC member and does not have to cut exports if the plan gets ACPC support.
"If we restrain our supplies, there are free riders in the region who will take our market," Paian Nainggolan, Indonesia's representative to the ACPC, said in mid-December.
